verses.text: These are the priests and Levites who came up with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua: Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra,
Amariah, Malluch, Hattush,
Shecaniah, Rehum, Meremoth,
Iddo, Ginnethoi, Abijah,
Mijamin, Maadiah, Bilgah,
Shemaiah, Joiarib, Jedaiah,
and Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, and Jedaiah. They were the leaders of the priests and their fellow priests in Jeshua's time.
The Levites included Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah. Mattaniah and his brothers led the songs of thanksgiving.
Their fellow Levites Bakbukiah and Unno stood next to them in their assigned places.
Jeshua was the father of Joiakim, Joiakim of Eliashib, and Eliashib of Joiada.
Joiada was the father of Jonathan, and Jonathan was the father of Jaddua.
In Joiakim's time, these priests headed their families: Meraiah led Seraiah's family, and Hananiah led Jeremiah's.
Meshullam led Ezra's family, and Jehohanan led Amariah's.
Jonathan led Malluchi's family, and Joseph led Shebaniah's.
Adna led Harim's family, and Helkai led Meraioth's.
Zechariah led Iddo's family, and Meshullam led Ginnethon's.
Zichri led Abijah's family. Miniamin's family was listed, and Piltai led Moadiah's.
Shammua led Bilgah's family, and Jehonathan led Shemaiah's.
Mattenai led Joiarib's family, and Uzzi led Jedaiah's.
Kallai led Sallai's family, and Eber led Amok's.
Hashabiah led Hilkiah's family, and Nethanel led Jedaiah's.
The heads of the Levite families were recorded in the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua, and the priests were recorded during the reign of Darius the Persian.
The heads of the Levite families were listed in the Book of the Chronicles through the time of Johanan son of Eliashib.
Hashabiah, Sherebiah, and Jeshua son of Kadmiel led the Levites. They and their fellow Levites stood group by group to give praise and thanks as David, the man of God, had commanded.
Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were gatekeepers who guarded the storerooms at the gates.
These men served in the days of Joiakim son of Jeshua, son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor and Ezra the priest and scribe.

At the dedication of Jerusalem's wall, the people called the Levites from wherever they lived to come to Jerusalem and celebrate the dedication with joy, with thanksgiving, singing, cymbals, stringed instruments, and harps.
The singers gathered from the plain around Jerusalem and from the villages of the Netophathites.
They also came from Beth Gilgal and the fields of Geba and Azmaveth, because they'd built villages for themselves around Jerusalem.
The priests and Levites purified themselves, then purified the people, the gates, and the wall.
I brought Judah's leaders up on the wall and appointed two large groups to give thanks and walk in procession. One group went to the right along the wall toward the Dung Gate.
Hoshaiah followed them with half of Judah's officials,
along with Azariah, Ezra, and Meshullam,
Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, and Jeremiah.
Some descendants of priests came with trumpets, including Zechariah son of Jonathan. His line went back through Shemaiah, Mattaniah, Micaiah, and Zaccur to Asaph.
His relatives Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani carried the musical instruments of David, the man of God. Ezra the scribe led them.
At the Spring Gate they went straight up the steps of the City of David, where the wall climbs above David's house, and continued east to the Water Gate.
The other group giving thanks went the opposite way to meet them. I followed with half the people along the wall, past the Tower of the Furnaces and on to the Broad Wall.
We went past the Ephraim Gate, the Old Gate, the Fish Gate, the Tower of Hananel, and the Tower of Hammeah, as far as the Sheep Gate. We stopped at the Guard Gate.
Both groups giving thanks then took their places in God's house. I was there with half the officials,
along with the priests Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah with trumpets,
and Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer. The singers sang loudly under the direction of Jezrahiah.
They offered many sacrifices that day and celebrated because God had given them great joy. The women and children celebrated too. Jerusalem's joy could be heard far away.

That day men were appointed over the storerooms for treasures, wave offerings, first produce, and tithes. They were to collect from the fields around the towns the portions the law assigned to the priests and Levites, because the people of Judah were glad for the priests and Levites who served.
The priests and Levites carried out the service of their God and the duties of purification. The singers and gatekeepers did their work too, as David and his son Solomon had commanded.
Long ago in the days of David and Asaph there was a leader of the singers, and there were songs of praise and thanksgiving to God.

In the days of Zerubbabel and Nehemiah, all Israel supplied what the singers and gatekeepers needed each day. They set aside the Levites' share, and the Levites set aside the share for Aaron's descendants.
